title: Traits Are Capabilities
goal: A trait names one thing a type can do. Bounds ask for exactly what the body uses.

sections.text: A trait names a capability. `Debug` means the type can be formatted with `{:?}`. `Display` means it has a user-facing text form for `{}`. `Clone` means it can be duplicated. A type only has the capabilities it implements, and using a missing one is error `E0277`.

sections.caption: derive writes the routine implementations for you.

sections.text: Many standard traits have mechanical implementations, and `#[derive(...)]` generates them: `Debug`, `Clone`, `Default`, `PartialEq`, and more. `Display` is deliberately not derivable, because user-facing formatting is a design decision. Writing an implementation by hand when a derive would produce the same code is flagged by Clippy's derivable_impls.

Generic functions request capabilities through bounds. The bound should match what the body actually uses: if the body formats with `{item}`, the bound is `T: Display` and nothing more. Asking for less does not compile. Asking for more, like adding `Clone` a body never uses, narrows who can call the function for no benefit.
The instinct for this deck: read what the body does, then grant or demand exactly that capability.

explanation: Traits name capabilities. Derive the mechanical ones, implement the meaningful ones, and bound generics by exactly what the body uses.
